item.description:
Workbench 2.7.0

Press Finish and your meeting is already written down; moments later it has a name. Copy it and go.

  • Finish, then Copy. Meetings confirms your call's words a phrase at a time while you talk, so Finish saves the transcript in about half a second instead of transcribing the whole call again (a 15-minute call used to take 12 seconds). The words are as accurate as before.
  • Every meeting has a name. Shortly after Finish, Apple Intelligence names the meeting and says in a line what it was about, with the decisions and next steps worth finding again. History, Home and Review transcript lead with that name; History has a Meetings filter and reads by day; and copying a meeting starts with its name, app, time and length, so meetings pasted together stay apart. Naming happens on your Mac and never changes your words; rename one in Details…, or turn naming off in Meetings' Recording options. Needs Apple Intelligence; otherwise meetings are named by their app.
  • Your words stay yours on laptop speakers. The other side's voice coming back through your microphone is now matched to the call and kept out of "You"; when it isn't clear, nothing is dropped. Quick replies like "Yes" keep every word, and short pauses no longer split what you said into new paragraphs.
  • Dictate sooner, even straight after an update. Your first live words show about 0.6 seconds after you start speaking, down from nearly 1.5. After Workbench or macOS updates, speech needs about 15 seconds to get ready: Dictate now starts recording at once and writes your words once speech is ready, instead of sending you to Models.
  • Meetings take half the space. Saved recordings are kept in Apple Lossless once their transcript is saved, every sample identical: an hour of a two-sided call should take about 400 MB instead of 800 MB. Recordings you already have are compressed quietly in the background.

Also in this release:

  • Follow up on any meeting. Prepare follow-up… is on every meeting in History, not only the newest, and ⌘F finds words in Review transcript.
  • Safari and FaceTime calls. Meetings offers a Safari call when macOS can tell it apart, and says so when it can't, before anything records. FaceTime and relayed iPhone calls record the call's audio.
  • Long meetings say when they'll finish. From 1 h 55 m the page, menu-bar panel and Home say when Workbench will finish the meeting, and a meeting Workbench ends itself says so and why in its notes.
  • Follow-ups you can trust. A failed follow-up can be run again from its meeting; one you stopped isn't re-sent unless you choose Retry… in History.
  • Snap's region crosshair appears a quarter of a second sooner.

When you're ready, update from General › Updates. Your saved work stays in this edition's library.

First download: unzip Workbench, move it to Applications in your home folder, then open it there. When replacing an existing copy, quit it and use the same Applications folder.

Workbench 2.6.0

Fewer surprises: every dictation, Snap and meeting now ends with your words kept and a plain answer about where they went.

  • Snaps stay sharp and easy to fix. Screen captures keep every Retina pixel. A new caption starts selected, so typing replaces "Your text", and Undo steps back one whole edit, not one keystroke. Copy says "Image copied" where you pressed it.
  • Dictation always tells you what happened. If a live insertion stops early or you cancel after words have landed, your words stay copied and the result says so where you acted, with Retry beside it. Light cleanup no longer deletes acronyms like ERM or UM, or mangles "Uh-huh".
  • Meetings hold up on long calls. A long call stays responsive with its page open and always saves. Plugging in headphones restarts only the audio that changed, so your microphone keeps recording. If no sound arrives from the call app, Meetings says why and where to allow it. ⌘Q while recording asks first.
  • Snap & Talk keeps your take. Quitting mid-narration keeps what you said and transcribes it once speech is ready. A retake that hears nothing keeps your earlier words, and Snaps you add join in the order you captured them.
  • Keys that tell the truth. A shortcut another app is holding shows as unavailable, and clears by itself once that app lets go. Every Change shortcut… opens Keyboard on that shortcut.

Also in this release:

  • Prepare follow-up… offers the Meeting notes and follow-up skill first, on the runner you've set up, and a meeting is handed off once.
  • Presenting is quieter. Present, Draw and Persona successes stop pinning orange lines in the menu-bar panel. The Timer keeps the display awake only while a countdown shows. Board export is reachable while a board is up.
  • Updates and installs explain themselves. An update that fails says why and what to do, and long prompts insert in seconds.
  • A fresh install reads as ready to set up, not as a failed speech setup, and History's Copy and Copy result confirm beside the button.

When you're ready, update from General › Updates. Your saved work stays in this edition's library.

First download: unzip Workbench, move it to Applications in your home folder, then open it there. When replacing an existing copy, quit it and use the same Applications folder.

Workbench 2.5.0

A Home worth opening, your phone on a clean stage, and a way to tell us when something goes wrong.

  • Home shows what's yours. Your latest meetings with the follow-up you prepared, your Snap & Talk decks (a sample deck shows until you build one), what this Mac lets Workbench use, and the keys worth learning next. Set up a permission from the same card, or change one in System Settings; Workbench asks only when you choose to. On a work Mac it says when an administrator has to switch something on, and Copy permission details gives your IT team what to allow.
  • Automatic paste, explained and on your layout. If automatic paste is off, the first copy says it needs Accessibility. Dictated words now paste with your keyboard layout's own ⌘V key, so Dvorak and Turkish F paste instead of sending another shortcut.
  • Learn your keys. Your keys shows your shortcuts on a keyboard and rings the next ones worth learning. Practice one, change it, or put Snap on ⌥G in one click. A key counts as learned once you've practised it or used it for real.
  • Present with your phone. Plug in your iPhone with a cable and it appears in the preview before you press Present. One line says what is happening and the one next step. If the phone doesn't appear, Can't see your phone? walks through the checks.
  • Report a problem. Choose Help › Report a Problem…, say what happened, and add a screenshot or a short voice note if it helps. The report goes privately to the Workbench team, and its receipt says when it was received. The same button sits beside a Dictate or Snap problem.
  • Every page, one way. Dictate, Meetings, Snap, Snap & Talk, Draw, History, Library, Persona and Settings share one set of cards, notes and a single primary action. A problem looks the same on every page, with its fix beside it.
  • The Mac's own menus. Hide Others, Show All, Zoom, Bring All to Front and Redo are where you expect them, and ⌘M minimises the window. Workbench reopens where you left it, and opening at login keeps it in the menu bar.

Also in this release:

  • History you can use again. Search saved work, review a transcript, and reuse it from the same place.
  • Meetings keep their words. Copy a finished transcript directly, and a recovered meeting keeps the text it had.
  • Dictation that fits. Words land with the spacing and capitals the insertion point needs, and names keep their capitals mid-sentence. Cancelling a paste leaves your transcript on the clipboard.
  • First speech setup you control. The model download is explicit and cancellable, and files already on this Mac are kept.
  • Library and Packs. Resources are easier to find, reuse and recover. Installed Packs work without setup.
  • Hand off without an assistant connected. Copy instructions carries the whole request, the selected text and the attachments to name, ready to paste into any assistant. Snap & Talk names the app it actually opened.
  • Updates in one click from the sidebar, with a line about what's new.
  • Persona: your camera and your photo, one click apart. Choose Persona leads with My Profile and Live Camera, and switching fades one into the other in place. React to my voice rings both. Live Camera offers Centre Stage where the camera supports it and opens Video Effects…, with gesture reactions off, so a thumbs-up mid-demo fires nothing. Connecting headphones while the ring listens can no longer stop Workbench.

What's gone or paused since 2.4.1:

  • Read is retired: its page, its voices and its Services menu item. Text you saved in Read is kept, word for word, in Library.
  • Switch to Browser Tab is paused. Saved links and browser settings are kept.
  • Present's gentle motion is retired, and a scene can no longer be set as your desktop picture. Restore desktop still puts back a picture Workbench applied earlier.
  • Library's From iPhone section and the photo handoff settings are gone; they never worked in the public app. Photos already saved on this Mac are untouched.

When you're ready, update from Settings: Workbench updates in 2.4.1, or General › Updates from 2.5.0 on. Your saved work stays in this edition's library.

First download: unzip Workbench, move it to Applications in your home folder, then open it there. When replacing an existing copy, quit it and use the same Applications folder.
